sections.markdown:
## C — Class D permits, examinations and medical reporting

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
The Class D Operator’s License covers passenger cars, station wagons, pickup trucks, utility vehicles and most panel trucks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Under the handbook’s Class D classification, the motor vehicle and trailer must have gross vehicle weight ratings no higher than 26,000 pounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
A Class D vehicle must be designed for fewer than 16 passengers when the driver is included in the count. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A Class D vehicle cannot be placarded for transporting hazardous materials. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A02
A Class D or Driving Privilege Card learner permit authorizes practice in the vehicle types covered by the corresponding operator license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A02
The Class D or Driving Privilege Card learner permit requires an accompanying properly licensed driver older than 21. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A02
The graduated learner permit covers Class D or Driving Privilege Card vehicles subject to the graduated-license program’s restrictions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A03
The driver examination evaluates the knowledge and driving skills needed for safe operation on Delaware roads. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A03
The handbook describes the driver examination as consisting of four parts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A03
Vision screening checks whether an applicant can see well enough to drive safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A03
If vision screening establishes a need for glasses or contacts, the license must state that the driver cannot legally drive without them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A03
Delaware’s minimum acceptable licensing vision is 20/40 with or without glasses or contacts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A03
The DMV may grant permission limited to daylight driving depending on the applicant’s vision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A04
The vision range specified for the daylight-driving category is between 20/40 and 20/50. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A04
The highway-sign test may require identifying a sign from its shape, color or symbol without its label. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A04
Applicants must explain the meanings of highway signs, traffic signals and pavement markings. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A04
Rules-of-the-road questions draw from Delaware road rules, motor-vehicle laws and safe-driving practices. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A04
A Class D applicant may take the road exam after 30 days have elapsed since passing the knowledge exam. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A04
The handbook permits road-exam scheduling through the DMV’s online scheduler or by calling a local DMV office. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A05
A road-exam applicant must bring a valid learner permit. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A05
The accompanying driver must bring a valid driver license and be at least 21 for the Class D road exam. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A05
The road-exam vehicle must have a valid registration card, including the trailer’s registration when applicable. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must supply a valid insurance card for the vehicle, either original or electronic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A05
The road exam requires approximately 30 minutes of driving. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A05
The road examiner will not ask the applicant to violate traffic law or safe-driving practices. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate appropriate responses to signs, signals and pavement markings. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate a three-point turn. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate right and left turns. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate lane changes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate application of right-of-way rules. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate control of appropriate driving speed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A05
The road-exam applicant must demonstrate backing for 50 feet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

Misconceptions: Road-test duration does not establish the knowledge-test time limit.
Mnemonics: Use “scope, sight, signs, skills” as an authored cue for sorting the cited licensing and examination topics.
Glossary: GVWR means gross vehicle weight rating; Class D is the operator-license category described in the cited handbook page.
Dynamic facts: Office schedules, appointment links and contact details require current confirmation and are withheld from stable facts.
